core_territory: Uzbekistan: Fergana, Andijan and Namangan Regions (the valley's namesake territory and its most populous stretch). Kyrgyzstan: Osh Region, Jalal-Abad Region and Batken Region (the valley's Kyrgyz rim, and the region holding nearly all of its named exclaves). Tajikistan: Sughd Region's southwestern Isfara/Konibodom edge specifically, not the whole region.
domain_territory: (none — this sphere is fully described by its core territory; unlike the mainland Southeast Asia spheres, the valley does not fade into a wider penumbra beyond the three countries and regions named)
sphere_territory: (none — fully contained within this map's three countries; the valley does not extend into any territory this project has already mapped elsewhere)
confidence: high (the valley's extent, ethnic mosaic, and the fact of the enclaves); medium (the exact regional-boundary attribution — Sughd's Isfara District as the Tajik-side valley edge is this file's own reading of the frameworks survey's Vorukh/Isfara reference, not an enumerated boundary in either survey)
notes: ⚠️ READ THE README'S DEDICATED ENCLAVE SECTION BEFORE DRAWING THIS ROW. This sphere captures the valley's broad, diffuse ethnolinguistic and settlement-pattern continuity (Uzbek/Tajik/Kyrgyz populations living intermixed across a shared agricultural basin) — it does NOT capture the eight literal point-enclaves (Sokh, Shakhimardan, Chon-Gara, Tash-Tepa, Vorukh, Kairagach and others) that this project's whole-first-order-subdivision rule cannot resolve into ordinary territory. Those are a separate, non-sphere drawing problem — see the README's "The Fergana Enclaves" section, the same structural role the Wa's hatched non-territory occupies in the Mainland Southeast Asia package. Draw this sphere as a broad overlay across the six named regions; draw the enclaves as individual point markers with leader lines, layered on top.

sphere_name: The Uyghur Diaspora / East Turkestan Reach
core_territory: (none — the ethnic core is Xinjiang/East Turkestan itself
domain_territory: outside this map's scope and already mapped as its own separate polity on this project's East Asia map series)
sphere_territory: Kazakhstan (~300,000–306,000 Uyghurs, concentrated in the southeast near the Chinese border). Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan (~50,000–60,000 each, estimates likely undercounted given long-standing cross-border intermarriage and integration).
source_section: Named but out of scope for this map — Xinjiang/East Turkestan itself. Do not draw territory here; label only if the map's extent reaches that far, and note that this project's East Asia survey has already settled Xinjiang/East Turkestan as never joining the Sinian Federation and remaining its own separate polity.
notes: high (the population estimates themselves); low (whether this diaspora presence should be drawn as a sphere at all — the frameworks survey raises this explicitly as an open question, not a decided design element, unlike S1)
column9: ⚠️ THE AUTHOR'S CALL, MORE SO THAN ANY OTHER ROW IN THIS FILE. The frameworks survey (§8.2) raises this explicitly without answering it: "should a Uyghur/East Turkestan cultural sphere overlay extend into Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan the way this project has used sphere overlays elsewhere?" This row exists as a drawable option, following the same "named but out of scope" convention the Mainland Southeast Asia package's Tai Continuum sphere already established for its own reach into southern China — but the author may reasonably prefer to omit this sphere entirely from the rendered map if a scattered diaspora population reads as a different kind of thing than a homeland-spanning ethnolinguistic continuum like S1 or the Tai Continuum. Tajikistan is deliberately not listed in domain_territory — the frameworks survey names only Kazakhstan's, Uzbekistan's and Kyrgyzstan's Uyghur populations, not Tajikistan's.
